subject: PII handling for prompt outputs — scope & retention confirmation
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <em@cerebrohealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-25T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: PII handling for prompt outputs — scope & retention confirmation

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the items we agreed to confirm in writing so your security and legal teams have a single reference:  

1) What you asked us to confirm
- Which categories of PII can appear in prompts/outputs that Cerebro is comfortable with Redwood storing for a limited time (e.g., patient identifiers, full DOB, free-form notes).
- Maximum retention for prompts vs generated outputs and the ability to disable retention.
- Level of logging (raw prompts, hashed identifiers, debug traces) and access controls.
- Data residency requirement: primary storage in the US; copies in EU-only region for EU patients.
- Evidence requested: SOC 2 Type II, encryption/KMS details, and an audit log sample.

2) Our commitments (high level) — will follow up with written detail and links:
- Default hosted behavior: prompts and metadata retained for up to 30 days for quality, billing, and troubleshooting; generated outputs are ephemeral by default (7 days) unless otherwise configured.
- We support a retention-disable option and a private deployment pattern (VPC/on-prem) that meets zero-retention needs.
- Logs: we can provide request-level metadata and cryptographic hashes of prompts instead of storing raw prompt text on request.
- Residency: we can pin customer data to a single region (US or EU) on Dedicated/Private plans; hosted accounts can be scoped to region on request.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a short note with exact TTLs and the SOC 2 link (attached).
- If acceptable, schedule a 30–45 minute technical follow-up with your infra/security folks to run through the data flow and configuration options (can include our compliance engineer).

Attached: redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf (high-level controls + toggles).

If anything above is off from your notes, flag it and I’ll update.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <em@cerebrohealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cerebro Health Legal <legal@cerebrohealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PII handling for prompt outputs — scope & retention confirmation

Mateo —

Thanks for the summary, that matches our internal notes. A few clarifications and mandatory items from Legal & Security:  

- Retention windows: Cerebro requires that raw prompts containing PHI are not retained longer than 30 days; generated outputs that include PHI must be deletable on request and should default to no more than 7 days.
- Option to disable: We need an option to opt-out of any prompt persistence entirely for our production environment (i.e., zero retention).
- Logs: only non-reversible hashes may be stored for troubleshooting; raw debug dumps may only be retained in a time-limited secure staging environment under strict access controls.
- Residency: EU patient data must be stored and processed in an EU region; US patient data in the US. Cross-region copies not allowed for patient-identifiable payloads.
- KMS: keys must be customer-managed for any environment marked as containing PHI.
- Evidence: please share a current SOC 2 Type II report, encryption-at-rest/in-transit documentation, and a recent audit-log excerpt (redacted ok).

Attaching our DPA request (cerebro-dpa-request-v1.pdf) for your review.

Elena
Director, Product Security
Cerebro Health

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are the specific configuration options and our recommended mappings so your engineers and legal can pick what fits best:  

1) Hosted (standard) — quick summary- Prompts: default retention 30 days; can be shortened to 0 days via a "no-persist" flag on the account level for inference traffic.
- Outputs: default ephemeral TTL 7 days; can be configured to 0 days.
- Logs: request metadata (timestamps, model id, token usage) retained; raw prompts may be replaced with salted SHA-256 hashes on request.

2) Dedicated / Private deployment — when zero tolerance required- Full support for region pinning (US-only or EU-only) and customer-managed KMS.
- No cross-region copies of PII by configuration.
- Option to disable all prompt persistence at the runtime level (KV cache is in-memory only and not checkpointed unless debug mode is enabled — and debug snapshots are only created with explicit opt-in).

3) Evidence and artifacts we can share today- SOC 2 Type II report (redwood-soc2-202707.pdf) — attached.
- High-level data flow diagram and retention table (see attached redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf).
- We can produce a redacted audit-log sample and a list of our access-control roles for the technical call.

4) Proposed next steps- Technical sync (30–45m) with your infra/security + our compliance engineer: available windows Wed/Thu next week.
- Legal: exchange DPA drafts; we can take your DPA and do a redline pass.

If you want the SOC 2 and DPA routed to Aditya (cc'ed) and our contracts team directly, I’ll loop them into the DocuSign exchange.

Thanks — I’ll also add a short appendix below mapping the exact TTLs for the options you requested.

Appendix: TTL quick map- Hosted default: prompts = 30d, outputs = 7d
- Hosted (no-persist flag): prompts = 0d, outputs = 0–7d (configurable)
- Dedicated/Private: retention configurable to customer policy (0d supported)

Best,
Mateo
